query: nomination registration requirements Section 60 Land Development Ordinance

documents.query: nomination registration requirements Section 60 Land Development Ordinance
documents.document_text: Section 60 states 'No nomination or cancellation of the nomination of a successor shall be valid unless the document effecting such nomination or cancellation is duly registered before the date of the death of the owner of the holding or the permit holder.' The question is whether the particular nomination of succession indicated in the original permit needs to be registered under Section 60.

query: permit holder succession endorsement before issue Section 87

documents.query: permit holder succession endorsement before issue Section 87
documents.document_text: Section 87 provides 'A person to whom a Government Agent has agreed to alienate land may nominate as his successor any person who is entitled under this Ordinance to be nominated, and the name of such successor may be endorsed on the permit before it is issued.' If the particular nomination was endorsed by the government agent before it is issued to the permit holder, there is no requirement that it should be registered under the Land Development Ordinance.

query: judicial review illegality unreasonableness public authority decisions

documents.query: judicial review illegality unreasonableness public authority decisions
documents.document_text: By 'illegality' as a ground for judicial review I mean that the decision maker must understand correctly the law that regulates his decision making power and must give effect to it. By 'irrationality' I mean what can be referred to as 'Wednesbury unreasonableness' - a decision which is so outrageous in its defiance of logic that no sensible person could have arrived at it. The Respondents have wrongly applied the provisions of the Land Development Ordinance.

query: land succession devolution Third Schedule priority rules

documents.query: land succession devolution Third Schedule priority rules
documents.document_text: Section 72 provides that when no successor has been nominated or the successor nominated has failed to succeed, the title to the land devolves as prescribed in Rule 1 of the Third Schedule. The said Rule provides for the relatives from whom the successor may be nominated. In the particular Schedule, preference is given to the oldest child as the successor. However, through amendment Act No.11 of 2022, preference is given to the person who developed such land over the older person.

query: ultra vires public decision making procedural fairness

documents.query: ultra vires public decision making procedural fairness
documents.document_text: The fundamental principle of judicial review is that the courts will intervene to ensure that the powers of public decision-making bodies are exercised lawfully. If the decision-maker exercises his powers outside the jurisdiction conferred, in a manner which is procedurally irregular or is Wednesbury unreasonable, he is acting ultra vires his powers and therefore unlawfully. The Respondents took steps to alter the records without giving the Petitioner any hearing.

query: social media contempt proceedings evidence requirements

documents.query: social media contempt proceedings evidence requirements
documents.document_text: The Criminal Investigations Department ('CID') has investigated the matter and ascertained that this article was uploaded to social media by the said Respondent. The said article had been circulated approximately among 122 web users and shared roughly among 4300 readers. Evidence was led through digital forensic investigation of computers taken into custody by the CID.

As the CID informed Court that the Respondent is absconding, the Attorney General moved that the matter be taken up for Inquiry in the absence of the Respondent. The Respondent has left the island while the relevant Magistrate's Court case was pending against him. This Court was convinced that sufficient evidence was led to establish that the Respondent is evading Court and decided to proceed with the Inquiry in the absence of the said Respondent.

query: burden of proof contempt of court criminal standard

documents.query: burden of proof contempt of court criminal standard
documents.document_text: The Supreme Court has observed that even if contempt is not always a crime, it bears a criminal character and therefore, it must be satisfactorily proved. Tilakawardena J. has held that the offence of contempt of court under our law is a criminal charge and the burden of proof is that of proof beyond reasonable doubt. We hold that the charges against the Accused have been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

The charge of contempt of Court was classically defined as the scandalizing of the Court, in that the words or acts are likely to bring the Court and the Judges into disrepute.
